incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a subset of the company's data environment; initial entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Employee, customer, and partner records were copied from a vendor serving 2,000+ US hospitals and ~10,000 clinics and pharmacies; reported to the FBI and UK ICO, with the intrusion contained and hospital services not disrupted.

incidents.victim: South Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Korea National Diplomatic Academy
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a previously unknown zero-day in server software plus misconfigured security settings on the academy e-learning platform, undetected for roughly nine to ten months.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole IDs, names, emails, and encrypted passwords of current and former MoFA employees and diplomatic trainees; the compromised system was shut down and not restored.

incidents.victim: Siemens ROX II (Ruggedcom) OT switch operators
incidents.vector: A chain of three zero-days (CVE-2025-40948 arbitrary file read, CVE-2025-40947 command-injection privilege escalation, CVE-2025-40949 persistent root via task scheduler) in Siemens ROX II industrial switches.
incidents.impact: Researcher-discovered chain (CVSS up to 9.1) that would give an attacker full root and reboot-persistent control of critical OT network switches; Siemens patched in firmware V2.17.1 with no known in-the-wild exploitation.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack reaching Fairlife production-related systems, disclosed in a Coca-Cola SEC filing.
incidents.impact: Production was halted at Fairlife's US factories; Canadian production lines were unaffected and no group has publicly claimed the attack.

incidents.vector: An unauthenticated SQL injection in WordPress core, reachable via the REST API, that chains to remote code execution.
incidents.impact: A core-level (not plugin) unauthenticated RCE affecting an extremely widely deployed CMS; a patch was released for 6.9/7.0 but the broad install base creates significant mass-exploitation risk.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle E-Business Suite servers as part of a broad extortion campaign against Oracle EBS customers.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen and disclosed to US state officials nearly a year late; the incident is the company's second breach following a 2023 compromise.

incidents.vector: Intrusion attributed by researchers to a China-based financially motivated group; technical details are limited.
incidents.impact: Reported compromise of a major certificate authority, an inherently high-trust, supply-chain-significant target; scope of any certificate or data impact remains unclear.

incidents.victim: Individuals and enterprises in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: Trojanized software installers (MobaXterm, WebEx, Zoom, DBeaver, FACEIT) delivered via ClickFix social engineering and weaponized HTA files that drop a Python 'Starland RAT' and PowerShell 'WLDR' C2 implant.
incidents.impact: The UAT-11795 campaign steals credentials, browser data, and cryptocurrency wallets and establishes persistent C2 (with a Polygon smart contract as fallback) to deliver follow-on payloads such as CastleStealer and Remcos.

incidents.victim: Western and regional critical infrastructure, ICS operators, and dissidents
incidents.vector: AI-accelerated spearphishing, ICS reconnaissance, and wiper/malware development by IRGC-linked units and state-aligned proxies during the 2026 conflict.
incidents.impact: AI is acting as a force multiplier scaling Iran's cyber, influence, and ICS-targeting operations, including reported sabotage of an Israeli industrial refrigeration system and campaigns against MENA targets and Iranian activists.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering lures leading to WebDAV/MSHTA-delivered PowerShell and Python loaders, with in-memory execution, steganography, and blockchain (EtherHiding) dead-drop C2 resolution.
incidents.impact: ACR Stealer campaigns harvested browser credentials, session tokens, and enterprise documents from OneDrive/SharePoint, enabling account compromise and follow-on intrusion.

incidents.victim: Nuclear Power Corp. of India / Kudankulam plant (via contractor Reliance Infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Third-party contractor breach (suspected exposed RDP, phishing, or a Fortinet flaw); a suspected ransomware execution was blocked by the data-center provider.
incidents.impact: About 19,000 files (14.3 GB) of engineering drawings and supplier/inspection documents for reactor Units 3-4 were published; India says they relate only to non-nuclear 'Balance of Plant' infrastructure with no safety systems affected.

incidents.vector: An attacker used an autonomous AI agent to exploit a code-execution flaw in the platform's data-processing pipeline via a malicious dataset, then pivoted internally.
incidents.impact: Internal datasets and some cloud/cluster credentials were stolen (no customer data exposed); notably, Hugging Face's own AI incident-response tooling was blocked by its guardrails, forcing a switch to local models.

incidents.vector: BEC phishing impersonating FedEx and other logistics firms delivers an obfuscated JavaScript attachment that drops a legitimate Lua/AutoIt interpreter plus a fake .ttf font file containing encrypted Lua bytecode for fileless, in-memory execution.
incidents.impact: The 'TFF Trap' campaign deploys RATs and infostealers (Agent Tesla, Remcos, XWorm) with low detection rates, enabling system takeover and credential/data theft for follow-on attacks.

incidents.victim: Organizations running on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server
incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, and CVE-2026-56164 for remote code execution, followed by theft of IIS machine keys and deserialization for persistence.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation grants unauthorized access to on-prem SharePoint; all three CVEs were added to CISA's KEV catalog, and post-exploit machine-key theft enables re-compromise even after patching.

incidents.vector: Actively exploited zero-days in the July 2026 Patch Tuesday, including CVE-2026-56155 (Active Directory Federation Services elevation of privilege) alongside the exploited SharePoint flaw.
incidents.impact: A record-setting release (570-plus flaws, ~250 privilege-escalation bugs) with multiple zero-days under active exploitation; also included CVE-2026-48561, a 9.6-CVSS unauthenticated RCE in Microsoft Copilot (not yet exploited).

incidents.vector: SNMP scanning of internet-facing routers using default/common community strings, then SNMP Set-Requests instructing devices to copy configurations and exfiltrate them via TFTP, plus occasional exploitation of known Cisco flaws and Smart Install.
incidents.impact: A multi-nation joint advisory details a decade-plus FSB Center 16 campaign opportunistically compromising poorly configured routers to steal device configs and establish persistent access to critical-infrastructure networks.

incidents.victim: Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (ANCPI)
incidents.vector: Login with valid/leaked credentials plus known unpatched software vulnerabilities; after a failed extortion attempt the attacker wiped systems and backups.
incidents.impact: The e-Terra cadastral platform and agency email were down for about a week, halting property transactions nationwide; stolen credentials, internal documents, and e-Terra source code were put up for sale as the agency rebuilds from an offline backup.

incidents.victim: AsyncAPI npm ecosystem (developers, CI/CD, downstream services)
incidents.vector: A GitHub Actions 'pwn request' stole a privileged bot token, which was used to ride the project's trusted publishing pipeline and republish five poisoned package versions that execute at module-import time (bypassing --ignore-scripts).
incidents.impact: Compromised @asyncapi/specs and generator packages delivered a 'Miasma' second-stage runtime with C2 and persistence fetched via IPFS; consumers were urged to remove the versions, purge caches, and rotate all exposed credentials.

incidents.vector: Abuse of trusted OAuth relationships via vishing-driven consent to malicious connected apps, supply-chain compromise of integrations (Salesloft Drift, Gainsight), and misconfigured Salesforce guest/Aura access.
incidents.impact: Threat actors quietly enumerated and mass-exfiltrated CRM records across many tenants without triggering conventional sign-in alerts; related activity extended to a June 2026 incident at intelligence platform Klue.

incidents.victim: US businesses and critical infrastructure (ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: OFAC sanctioned enablers of ransomware crews, including a no-logs VPN service (1VPNS) used to hide attack origins and a seller of 'cryptors' that disguise ransomware to evade security tools.
incidents.impact: Two individuals and one entity were designated (coordinated with the UK) following a May 2026 takedown of 1VPNS infrastructure; the services underpinned ransomware operations causing billions in US losses.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited the platform's own price-reporting (oracle) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Roughly $18 million was stolen from the DeFi platform.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-Service using edge-device exploits, brute force, stolen credentials, and initial-access brokers, plus custom Go/C encryptors, an EDR-killer framework, and self-propagation across virtual infrastructure.
incidents.impact: 'The Gentlemen' RaaS has claimed 580-plus victims across 77 countries since inception (103 in manufacturing) and, fueled by a 90% affiliate payout, became the second most active ransomware program of 2026.

incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of 16-plus known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (WordPress plugins, Craft CMS, Joomla JCE, etc.) enabling unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF, and deserialization to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Attackers gain remote control of web servers for defacement, credential capture, and malware distribution, and use them as a foothold for broader network compromise; ACSC warns many Australian SMBs are affected.

incidents.vector: A Go-based backdoor ('GigaWiper') that consolidates multiple destructive payloads — physical-disk wiping, unrecoverable fake-ransomware encryption, and secure multi-pass wiping — as on-demand C2 commands over RabbitMQ/Redis.
incidents.impact: Since October 2025, Microsoft observed compromised environments wiped at the physical-disk level and rebooted, reflecting a shift toward modular, destruction-focused implants that carry real-world sabotage consequences.
